method: Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinates are Cartesian metres: X runs through the equator and prime meridian, Y through the equator at 90 degrees east, and Z through the north pole. The WGS84 ellipsoid uses a semi-major axis of 6378137 m and a flattening of 1/298.257223563, giving a semi-minor axis of 6356752.314245 m and a first eccentricity squared of 0.006694379990141316. Geodetic to ECEF uses N = a / sqrt(1 - e2 sin^2(lat)), X = (N + h) cos(lat) cos(lon), Y = (N + h) cos(lat) sin(lon) and Z = (N (1 - e2) + h) sin(lat), with h the ellipsoid height in metres. ECEF to geodetic takes p = sqrt(X^2 + Y^2), longitude = atan2(Y, X), and solves for the geodetic latitude with a fixed-point iteration started at atan2(Z, p (1 - e2)); the height is p / cos(lat) - N, or z / sin(lat) - N (1 - e2) close to the poles. An exact pole has no longitude, so it is reported as 0 degrees with the height |Z| - b, and an all-zero ECEF position is refused because the geodetic position is undefined at the Earth's centre. The geocentric latitude atan2(Z, p) is reported beside the geodetic latitude; the two differ by up to about 0.19 degrees at mid-latitudes. Angles and ECEF metres accept at most six and nine decimals respectively, ellipsoid height at most three, and every field is range-checked. The converter does not transform between datums, apply a geoid model, or convert orthometric height above sea level, and it cannot replace authoritative survey or navigation data. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: WGS84 defines a semi-major axis of 6378137 m and a flattening of 1/298.257223563.
Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed coordinates are right-handed Cartesian metres with X through the equator at the prime meridian, Y through the equator at 90 degrees east, and Z through the north pole.
Geodetic latitude is measured from the ellipsoid normal while geocentric latitude is measured from the Earth's centre; they differ by up to about 0.19 degrees at mid-latitudes.
Ellipsoid height is measured above the WGS84 ellipsoid and differs from orthometric height above mean sea level by the geoid undulation.
